title: Convention Plugins as Build Standards Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies convention plugins as build standards?
options: Expose small named build capabilities through cohesive tested convention plugins.
Create one plugin for all modules
Mutate subprojects from root after evaluation
questions.answer: Expose small named build capabilities through cohesive tested convention plugins.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: Convention plugins should always hard-code every setting so modules cannot override defaults.
questions.explanation: A single convention plugin that applies every tool to every module recreates global configuration under a new name and increases cost and coupling.

questions.prompt: Why are convention plugins preferable to subprojects blocks?
questions.answer: They make shared configuration explicit, composable, testable and applied only to modules declaring that capability.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
